title: One retry, one debit
summary: Make SQLite reservation retries durable and keep request outcome consistent with stock.

constraints: Preserve RetryInventory(path), seed, available, reserve(request_id, sku, quantity), and close; each instance owns its SQLite connection. Fixture seed occurs before requests; concurrent callers are outside this task.

Persist the exact request ID, payload and boolean outcome across reopen. Identical retry returns the original outcome without a second debit; changed payload under that ID raises ValueError unchanged.
A new accepted request decrements once; missing or insufficient stock records False without changing stock. Record request outcome and stock change in one durable transaction.

Validate non-empty string identifiers and exact positive integer reservation quantities before any change; booleans are invalid. Seed accepts exact non-negative integer stock. Preserve non-blank identifier text exactly.

rubric.name: Durable request identity
rubric.description: Keep exact retry identity and payload conflict semantics.

anchors.strong: Persists both success and failure outcomes, reproduces retries after reopen and rejects conflicts.
anchors.developing: Handles successful retry in memory but loses history or misses rejected identity.
anchors.needsWork: Debits again or silently changes a request payload.

rubric.name: Atomic failure consistency
rubric.description: Keep stock and outcome in the same durable transaction.

anchors.strong: Explains the transaction boundary and leaves state consistent across errors.
anchors.developing: Uses durable writes but cannot justify their combined failure behavior.
anchors.needsWork: Records success without a debit or debits without a matching durable outcome.

rubric.name: Retry regression evidence
rubric.description: Test reopen, conflict and rejected identity.

anchors.strong: Adds focused checks for durable retry and explains why sequential tests do not establish concurrency.
anchors.needsWork: Infers persistence or atomic failure safety from a single normal request.

probes.question: How does a reopened connection know whether a request already happened?
What partial state could appear if you commit the debit and result separately?
Which failure and reopen check would catch a duplicate debit?

hints: Separate retry identity from the resource being reserved.
A failed outcome still belongs to an exact request payload.
Put stock modification and new request outcome in one transaction; replay should read the prior outcome.
